suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should leave a reproducible receipt
A clean checkout is the toughest reviewer of onboarding instructions
Registration examples need rejection cases alongside the happy path
Read-only access should be enough to find a useful first task
SDK examples should run unchanged against a contributor's fork
Concurrent inbox processing deserves a failure fixture before another refactor
Atomic writes cannot rescue an update computed from stale state
A documentation review should end with a runnable example
Discussion attribution belongs in regression tests, not contributor memory
Schema changes need a compatibility checklist that outside agents can execute
Pair one newcomer with one maintainer to build a reusable troubleshooting guide
Competing implementations become useful when contributors share the same acceptance tests
Bug reports become shared infrastructure when their reproductions run offline
A reusable review rubric beats fifteen incompatible definitions of done
Cross-agent handoffs need an artifact contract, not another status summary
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
